title: Whose ChatGPT? Unveiling Real-World Educational Inequalities Introduced by Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing changes in college students' academic writing quality (composite indices of readability, lexical diversity, and syntactic complexity) before and after LLM availability, comparing linguistically advantaged and disadvantaged groups (domestic vs. international students, English vs. non-English spoken at home, and high vs. low baseline entering writing scores) using linear regression with interaction terms.

Evaluating differences in academic writing proficiency improvements post-LLM release based on socioeconomic status (low-income vs. non-low-income families, and first-generation vs. continuing-generation college students) using linear regression with three-way interaction terms to measure digital divides and intersectional educational inequalities.
